title: Repair initial held-input sampling in the selected SDL3 provider
goal: Repair the reproduced SDK cache-initialization gap where SDL reports already-held controls but the first assigned SDK user reads zeros, using an isolated reviewed provider profile while preserving every existing SDK package and input contract.
acceptance: Retain MW3-085's Windows/Linux held-discovery failures and actual SDL-versus-SDK values; audit provider creation, current-state reads, event normalization and threading before choosing the minimal repair

Use an original licensed patch and a separate derived source/build/cache/package from the verified XMA profile; initialize the provider snapshot without changing guest mappings, user assignment, kernel imports, generated code or another lane's SDK

Bind exact parent/source/patch/compiler/configuration/library identities and an explicit replacement allowlist; preserve unaffected files and parents, and split any broader SDK or interface repair before implementation

Admit the new profile explicitly in the two diagnostic runners while preserving default XMA behavior; these shared runner paths are serialized after completed 084/085, not edited during their active claims
Make the unchanged held-discovery correctness case pass with actual loaded repaired-library proof; never remove the assertion, count a known failure as success or add success-valued input stubs
validation: Compare retained baseline and repaired native Windows/Linux results with identical original stimuli; rerun all user-routing and raw-provider cases, including held controls, packet changes, all 24 attach orders, hotplug, UI blocking, virtual rumble, stale events and wrong-routing controls

Run supported host and participating-library sanitizers, independently reconcile actual loaded library/source/binary/receipt identities and cleanup, and document unavailable instrumentation and physical hardware explicitly

Reject stale parents, wrong patch/package/replacement identities, changed unaffected files and incomplete/late/wrong outputs; run public game-free checks and record performance impact without a title benchmark claim
size: bounded host-provider repair and isolated profile; no title service admission
